decisions.reason: A classic lever handle builds directly on the firm's core metalworking and hardware knowledge, so management can read its market results well and refine it at low cost.
A lever handle family fits the firm's established design and production expertise, and its early results are easy to interpret within the existing portfolio.
A new door handle design draws on related design knowledge the firm already holds, and one year is too short to judge its uptake, so keeping it allows further learning.
Like the other handle designs, it sits within the core competence, and the firm can adapt it from early feedback rather than withdraw it.
A handle family extends existing lines where the firm has strong absorptive capacity, which favours keeping it and refining it.

The electronic access system with its unique light technology stretches the firm's knowledge base, but as a large hardware maker it likely has in-house R&D and partners in electronics, so it should keep the product to build capability in this strategic growth area.
